title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
Amazon is investing $50 billion in OpenAI, signaling a major shift in the AI landscape alongside Elon Musk’s consolidation efforts involving SpaceX, Tesla, and xAI. A significant legal battle is unfolding with music publishers suing Anthropic for $3 billion over copyright infringement related to AI training data. Apple’s iPhone division achieved record sales, but questions remain about Tim Cook’s AI monetization strategy, and they’ve expanded AI capabilities through the acquisition of Q.ai. 

Microsoft continues to rely on Nvidia and AMD for AI chips, while Google unveiled its AI-world generator, Project Genie, and integrated Gemini into Google Maps. Waymo expanded its robotaxi services to San Francisco International Airport. 

Geopolitically, tensions remain high regarding Iran, with the EU adding the Revolutionary Guards to its terrorist list.  India is a key market for Google’s AI in education, and a dispute involving an Iranian-seized oil tanker is ongoing.  Domestically, President Trump filed a lawsuit against the IRS, and a bipartisan funding package was approved for Homeland Security. Cybersecurity concerns are highlighted by a data breach at Marquis, and a new AI lab, Flapping Airplanes, has launched.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
The Overnight Market Brief – Pre-Market Edition for January 29, 2026, provides a market overview following a mixed Wall Street close driven by the Federal Reserve’s decision to maintain steady rates. The 10-Year Treasury yield rose to 4.251%, while the US Dollar Index decreased to 96.095, alongside increases in Crude Oil (64.64) and Gold (5562.96).

Overnight, Asian markets, including a flat Nikkei 225, a 0.51% gain in the Hang Seng, and a 0.16% rise in the Shanghai Composite, benefited from the dollar’s decline. European markets exhibited caution due to weaker-than-expected Swedish GDP growth and a drop in UK vehicle production, alongside Chancellor Merz’s concerns about the dollar’s impact on German exports.

US futures are currently up, with S&P 500 futures rising 0.15% and Nasdaq 100 futures increasing 0.06%. Investors are focused on the Fed’s policy implications, currency market dynamics, and geopolitical developments, particularly regarding German exports and trade discussions. With a light economic calendar, market flows are expected to be influenced by technical positioning and these broader macro themes, suggesting a range-bound market with a slight upward bias.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
The Post-Market Recap by AGI Era presented a mixed market performance on Thursday, January 29, 2026, with the US session ending slightly bearish. The S&P 500 dipped 0.13% to 6969.01, while the Nasdaq 100 retreated 0.53% to 25884.295, driven by rotation out of tech. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 55.96 points to 49071.56, showcasing a divergence.

Trading volume was notably lower than average, suggesting tactical adjustments rather than a fundamental shift. The VIX rose 3.24% to 16.88, indicating cautious apprehension but not widespread panic. Sector performance highlighted a move towards defensive stocks, with Utilities (XLU) holding steady and Technology (XLK) lagging.

Bond market dynamics played a key role, with the 10-Year Treasury Yield remaining flat at 4.25%, reflecting the Fed’s “wait and see” approach. The US Dollar Index weakened slightly, while Crude Oil surged 3.24% due to a decline in natural gas storage.

Within the Magnificent Seven, Nvidia showed modest gains, while Microsoft plummeted 9.99%, and Tesla continued its downward trend. Meta’s surge of 10.44% offered a counterpoint, reflecting investor confidence. Analysts noted a more discerning approach among investors, focusing on individual company fundamentals.

Looking ahead, investors will be closely monitoring jobless claims, factory orders, and Federal Reserve commentary regarding interest rates and inflation.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary:
Escalating tensions dominated today’s geopolitical updates. U.S. President Trump issued a stark warning to Iran, stating the “time is running out” on a nuclear agreement, coinciding with a significant buildup of U.S. military assets in the Persian Gulf, raising international concerns. Iranian officials responded with a readiness to counter any aggression.

Meanwhile, U.K. Prime Minister Starmer concluded a diplomatic visit to China, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties despite domestic criticism. Tragically, a Russian drone strike resulted in five deaths in a crowded Ukrainian train, highlighting the ongoing human cost of the conflict. In Europe, Estonian Prime Minister Kallas urged EU member states to take greater responsibility for their defense, diverging from NATO’s reliance on the U.S.

Economically, Deutsche Bank faced raids as part of a money laundering investigation, and Amazon announced a massive job cut. South Korea’s former first lady was sentenced to prison on bribery charges. These events, combined with the volatile U.S.-Iran situation, paint a picture of a world grappling with multiple crises and shifting geopolitical alliances.
